translations.1: 《零重力咖啡杯》，由 Science@NASA 出品
translations.2: 在我们星球的高空，在卫星和空间站所在的领域，地球上那些熟悉的规则不再适用。
translations.3: 正午的天空像夜晚一样漆黑。
translations.5: 掉落的东西不会往下掉，热空气也不会往上升。
translations.6: 不过，在那里发生的所有怪事中，最奇怪的也许发生在咖啡身上。
translations.7: 在微重力环境下，一杯普通的早晨咖啡也能变成一次名副其实的“天外”体验。
translations.8: 波特兰州立大学的物理学教授马克·韦斯洛格尔对太空中的咖啡和其他流体做过很多思考，他描述了会发生什么。
translations.9: 他说，首先，光是把咖啡倒进杯子里就是件麻烦事。
translations.10: 没有了重力的牵引，倒液体会变得非常棘手。
translations.11: 不过，为了便于讨论，我们假设你在空间站上，手里拿着一杯咖啡。
translations.12: 最自然的做法是把杯子朝嘴边倾斜。
translations.13: 但当你这么做时，咖啡会非常难以控制。
translations.14: 事实上，它很可能根本不会动。
translations.15: 你得朝着自己的脸晃动杯子，希望有一些热液体能挣脱出来，飘到你嘴里。
translations.16: 往好处想，等杯子空了的时候，你大概已经完全清醒了。
translations.17: 在太空中“不守规矩”的液体可不只有咖啡。
translations.18: 低温燃料、热冷却剂、饮用水，还有尿液，也都是这样。
translations.19: 流体的行为是整个航天领域中最违反直觉的事情之一。
translations.20: 这给设计使用流体的航天器系统的工程师们带来了极大的挑战。
translations.21: “我们的直觉完全是错的，”韦斯洛格尔感叹道。
translations.22: “要猜测流体在新系统中会怎样表现时，我们常常一无所知。”
translations.23: 为了更好地了解微重力下的流体，韦斯洛格尔和同事们正在国际空间站上开展“毛细流动实验”。
translations.24: 例如，他们实验套件中的一个装置专门研究内角。
translations.25: 如果两个固体表面以足够小的角度相交，微重力下的流体就会自然地沿着接缝流动。
translations.27: 这种毛细效应可以用来引导各种流体在航天器中流动，从低温燃料到回收的废水都可以。
translations.28: 毛细驱动的流动在地球上很难研究，因为在地球上它会被重力削弱。
translations.29: 而在空间站上，大规模的角流却很容易产生和观察。
translations.30: 韦斯洛格尔和同事们已经凭借这项研究中发明的装置获得了三项专利。
translations.31: 一项是微重力冷凝换热器。
translations.32: 另一项描述了一种能分离并控制多相流体的装置。
translations.33: 第三项专利是——你猜对了——一个低重力咖啡杯。
translations.34: 宇航员唐·佩蒂特在空间站工作期间参与过毛细流动实验，他帮助发明了这个杯子，并与韦斯洛格尔共同拥有这项专利，
translations.35: 共同拥有专利的还有两位数学家保罗·康卡斯和罗伯特·芬恩，他们对这一现象做了最早的理论分析。
translations.36: 简单来说，杯子的一侧有一个尖锐的内角。
translations.37: 在空间站的微重力环境中，毛细力会让液体沿着这条槽道流动，一直送到喝的人嘴边。
translations.38: 你小口啜饮时，液体会不断流过来，让你在失重环境中也能享用咖啡。
translations.39: “能一直喝到最后一滴，”佩蒂特说。
translations.40: 未来的太空移民想要庆祝时，用的很可能就是这种杯子。
translations.41: 事实上，这项专利申请特别提到，举杯祝酒就是这个装置的用途之一。
translations.42: 不难想象他们可能会为什么而干杯。
translations.43: 厕所、空调、燃料箱和回收系统，都因为空间站上的毛细流动实验而运转得更好。
translations.44: 想了解更多关于太空旅行中那些日常奇事的新闻，请访问 science.nasa.gov。

vocab.def_en: an area of activity, interest, or knowledge; a domain
vocab.example: Quantum physics is outside the realm of everyday experience.

vocab.def_en: well known to you because you have seen or experienced it often
vocab.example: It was nice to see a familiar face at the party.

vocab.def_en: to be relevant to or have an effect on someone or something
vocab.example: These rules apply to all students.

vocab.def_en: a condition of very weak gravity, as experienced in orbit
vocab.example: Plants grow in strange directions in microgravity.

vocab.def_en: a substance that can flow, such as a liquid or gas
vocab.example: Drink plenty of fluids when you have a cold.

vocab.def_en: a task that is boring or unpleasant but has to be done
vocab.example: Washing the dishes is my least favorite chore.

vocab.def_en: difficult to do or deal with; needing care and skill
vocab.example: Parking in this narrow street can be tricky.

vocab.def_en: used when you suggest something only so that it can be discussed, even if it may not be true
vocab.def_zh: 为了便于讨论；姑且假设
vocab.example: Let's say, for the sake of argument, that the plan costs nothing.

vocab.def_en: to move so that one side is higher than the other; to tilt
vocab.example: She tipped her chair back and looked at the ceiling.

vocab.def_en: to escape or become free from something that holds you
vocab.example: The boat broke loose from its rope during the storm.

vocab.def_en: completely awake; fully alert
vocab.example: After two cups of coffee, I was wide awake.

vocab.def_en: to behave badly; (of a thing) to not work in the normal or expected way
vocab.example: My laptop starts to misbehave when it gets too hot.

vocab.def_en: relating to or kept at extremely low temperatures
vocab.example: Rockets often burn cryogenic liquid hydrogen.

vocab.def_en: a liquid or gas used to keep a machine or engine cool
vocab.example: Check the coolant level before a long drive.

vocab.def_en: (of water) safe to drink
vocab.example: The village finally has a supply of potable water.

vocab.def_en: not easy to understand or predict by instinct; going against common sense
vocab.example: The app's menu is so unintuitive that nobody can find the settings.

vocab.def_en: to create a problem, danger, or difficulty
vocab.example: Rising sea levels pose a serious threat to coastal cities.

vocab.def_en: the ability to know or understand something without conscious reasoning
vocab.example: My intuition told me something was wrong.

vocab.def_en: to express sadness or regret about something
vocab.example: Many fans lamented the end of the series.

vocab.def_en: not knowing about something; uninformed
vocab.example: The staff were kept in the dark about the merger.

vocab.def_en: to organize and carry out an activity, such as research or a survey
vocab.example: The team conducted a survey of 500 customers.

vocab.def_en: relating to the way a liquid moves through very narrow spaces because of surface tension
vocab.example: Capillary action lets water climb up a paper towel.

vocab.def_en: to make something weaker or less strong
vocab.example: The rain did not dampen the fans' excitement.

vocab.def_en: to officially give someone something they have asked for
vocab.example: She was granted a visa to study in Canada.

vocab.def_en: an official right to be the only one who can make, use, or sell an invention for a period of time
vocab.example: The company holds more than 200 patents.

vocab.def_en: a fact or event that can be observed, especially one that is unusual or interesting
vocab.example: Rainbows are a natural phenomenon caused by sunlight and rain.

vocab.def_en: to drink something slowly, taking very small amounts
vocab.example: He sat by the window, sipping his tea.

vocab.def_en: having no weight, or seeming to have no weight, as in space
vocab.example: Astronauts float around because they are weightless.

vocab.def_en: a person who settles in a new place, especially to form a community there
vocab.example: The first colonists on Mars will need to grow their own food.

vocab.def_en: to raise glasses and drink together to honor someone or celebrate something
vocab.example: We toasted the bride and groom with champagne.
